content: The American Diabetes Association emphasizes the importance of routine monitoring of albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in diabetic patients. This practice is critical for identifying the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and managing associated complications effectively. Elevated levels of albuminuria and changes in eGFR serve as significant biomarkers for assessing the risk of CKD, enabling the early detection of kidney disease. It is recommended that these parameters be monitored on an annual basis, or more frequently in patients who are at higher risk. This approach facilitates timely medical interventions and adjustments to treatment regimens as needed.
